# Aunt Euphemia

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000), [v3 c9 P13](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0013)</sub>
- **Role:** Housekeeper  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000), [v3 c26 P14](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0014)</sub>
- **Titles:** Aunt Euphemia  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000)</sub>; Aunt Phemie  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000)</sub>; Aunty J.  <sub>[v3 c24 P15](../source/v03-c24.md#nw-v03-c24-p0015)</sub>

## Appearance

Aunt Euphemia is a small, elderly woman with a gently triangular face, rose-colored cheeks, and large, tender blue eyes full of youth. She has silver-white hair arranged in soft rolls over her ears. She dresses in an outmoded style.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)_

## Personality

She possesses a cheerful, indulgent, and irrepressible nature. She is fond of humor and does not take herself or life's minor troubles too seriously, preferring to let young people enjoy themselves rather than strictly supervise them. Although she claims her views are old-fashioned, she maintains a remarkably youthful spirit and a sharp, witty perspective.

_Sources: [v3 c16 P51](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0051), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c22 P3](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0003), [v3 c26 P21](../source/v03-c26.md#nw-v03-c26-p0021)_

## Goals

- Keep house for Mabel Colby, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay at Tabby's Place  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000), [v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014)</sub>
- Travel to India to inspect her daughter's mission field  <sub>[v3 c35 P1](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0001)</sub>

## History

Aunt Euphemia was left alone in a large house when her daughter married and departed for missionary work. Mabel Colby proposed that she come to Portmaris to keep house at Tabby's Place for Mabel, Nell Harcourt, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay during their final years at Wexcombe College. She agreed and moved to Portmaris, bringing along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. During her time at Tabby's Place, she provided a warm, comfortable, and indulgent home for the students. After the girls graduated from college, she chose to remain in the house for the summer to care for the cats rather than visit relatives, before eventually traveling to India to visit her daughter's mission field.

_Sources: [v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000), [v3 c9 P14](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0014), [v3 c16 P0](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0000), [v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053), [v3 c16 P56](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0056), [v3 c35 P1](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0001)_

## Background by volume

- Was named Jamesina after her father James, who drowned at sea prior to her birth  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000)</sub>
- Her only daughter married and left for a foreign mission field in India  <sub>[v3 c9 P0](../source/v03-c09.md#nw-v03-c09-p0000)</sub>
- Had many suitors in her youth, though she never remarried after her husband's death  <sub>[v3 c35 P22](../source/v03-c35.md#nw-v03-c35-p0022)</sub>
- Her daughter holds a Master of Arts degree  <sub>[v3 c37 P14](../source/v03-c37.md#nw-v03-c37-p0014)</sub>

## Quotes

> If you will ever understand how to conduct yourselves, you are at an age to know it now. Therefore, as it pertains to me, you are all free to ruin yourselves as you see fit.  <sub>[v3 c16 P53](../source/v03-c16.md#nw-v03-c16-p0053)</sub>

> A person can easily catch rheumatism in her legs, Nell. However, solely the elderly ought to experience soul rheumatism. Fortunately, I have escaped it entirely. Once your soul is afflicted with rheumatism, you may as well proceed to select your coffin.  <sub>[v3 c25 P10](../source/v03-c25.md#nw-v03-c25-p0010)</sub>

> Fulfill what you owe to God, to those around you, and to yourself, while enjoying your life. Such is the doctrine I live by, and it has served me quite effectively.  <sub>[v3 c22 P3](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0003)</sub>
